issues.label: Banking Crisis
issues.summary: Systemic failure of commercial banking institutions. Loan losses exceed capital buffers, depositor confidence collapses, and the credit intermediation function freezes. Bank failures cascade through interbank lending networks. The real economy loses access to credit, producing recession or depression.

circuits.detail: Commercial banking relay function collapses as loan losses erode capital, credit intermediation freezes, and the economy loses its primary capital routing mechanism
Central bank forced into emergency mode â€” slashing rates, expanding balance sheet, and providing emergency lending to prevent total system collapse
Credit allocation systems freeze as banks refuse to lend even to creditworthy borrowers, producing credit crunch that strangles business investment and consumer spending
Mortgage markets collapse as property valuations crash, underwater homeowners default, and securitized mortgage products transmit losses across the global financial system
Regulatory monitoring failed to detect risk accumulation before crisis, revealing supervisory gaps in risk assessment, capital adequacy enforcement, and systemic interconnection mapping
Risk management models failed catastrophically, with executives and boards unable to comprehend or control the complex exposures their institutions had accumulated

issues.label: Market Crash
issues.summary: Rapid and severe decline in asset prices across equity, bond, or commodity markets. Panic selling overwhelms market-making capacity, liquidity evaporates, and price discovery breaks down. Wealth destruction triggers negative feedback loops into consumer confidence and business investment.

circuits.detail: Stock market reward valuation collapses as investor sentiment shifts from greed to panic, producing indiscriminate selling that destroys price-discovery function
Derivatives amplify losses through leveraged positions, margin calls trigger forced liquidation, and complex instruments become impossible to value as markets seize
Private equity and institutional investor valuations become unreliable as mark-to-market accounting reveals previously hidden losses across portfolio companies
Risk management capacity overwhelmed as models designed for normal conditions fail in extreme stress, with correlation assumptions breaking down precisely when they matter most
Regulatory alarm triggers emergency interventions â€” trading halts, short-selling bans, and emergency liquidity injections as regulators scramble to contain cascading failure

issues.label: Currency Collapse
issues.summary: Rapid devaluation of a national currency destroying purchasing power, savings, and international trade capacity. Capital flight, hyperinflation, and import collapse devastate the real economy. Sovereign debt denominated in foreign currency becomes unpayable.

circuits.detail: Forex market attention overwhelms the collapsing currency with massive sell pressure as traders and capital flee to safe-haven currencies
Central bank monetary homeostasis fails â€” either through policy error (excessive money printing) or external shock that overwhelms monetary policy capacity
Bond market confidence collapses as sovereign creditworthiness is destroyed, with government unable to borrow at any sustainable interest rate
Payment systems disrupted as merchants refuse depreciating currency, dollarization emerges informally, and the domestic monetary unit loses its transaction medium function
Credit systems become dysfunctional as lenders cannot price loans in a currency with unpredictable future value, freezing both consumer and commercial lending
Commercial banking relay breaks down as banks face currency mismatches on their balance sheets and depositors withdraw savings in panic

issues.label: Credit Freeze
issues.summary: Systemic seizure of lending activity. Banks refuse to extend credit to businesses and consumers despite adequate capital. Interbank lending markets freeze as institutions distrust each other's solvency. Economic activity dependent on credit â€” which is nearly all of it â€” grinds to a halt.

circuits.detail: Credit allocation systems shut down entirely as banks hoard cash, refuse new lending, and tighten existing credit lines regardless of borrower quality
Banking relay function frozen â€” deposits accumulate but are not transmitted to borrowers, breaking the intermediation chain that funds economic activity
Central bank forced into unconventional monetary policy (quantitative easing, negative rates) to unfreeze credit channels that conventional rate cuts cannot reach
Venture capital and growth investment motivation collapses as risk appetite evaporates and investors retreat to cash and government bonds
Mortgage origination freezes as lenders refuse to extend long-term property loans, collapsing housing markets and construction activity

issues.label: Systemic Contagion
issues.summary: Failure cascading across interconnected financial institutions. One institution's collapse triggers counterparty losses that exceed capital buffers of connected institutions, producing domino-effect failures. Too-big-to-fail and too-connected-to-fail institutions hold the entire system hostage.

circuits.detail: Banking relay network becomes the contagion pathway â€” interbank lending connections that normally distribute liquidity instead transmit failure from institution to institution
Payment system infrastructure threatened as clearing and settlement institutions face counterparty failures, risking collapse of the transaction processing backbone
Derivative counterparty chains amplify contagion â€” one institution's failure triggers margin calls and counterparty losses across hundreds of connected entities simultaneously
Regulatory systems overwhelmed by simultaneous failures across multiple institutions, with crisis management capacity exhausted and coordination between agencies breaking down
Insurance sector faces catastrophic claims as credit default swaps and financial guarantees are triggered simultaneously, threatening insurer solvency and deepening the cascade

_marketContext._comment: ADDITIVE metadata (does not alter activations/edges). Separates broad-market MACRO ANCHORS from individual PLAYER NODES so analysts never conflate company-level alpha (a single bank's strategy/earnings) with macro-level beta (aggregate investor expectation of economic growth). A JPM stock move is NOT a macro signal; an SPY move IS. Finance stays DISTINCT from the 'economy' domain: economy owns the MACRO AGGREGATE (GDP/CPI/employment/policy via FRED series); finance owns CAPITAL MARKETS / CREDIT / BANKS. These broad-market proxies anchor capital-market activations to macroeconomic conditions WITHOUT importing economy's FRED macro indicators.

macroAnchors.name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF

macroAnchors.name: SPDR Gold Shares
macroAnchors.reflects: Risk-off / safe-haven sentiment and real-rate / currency-debasement fears; a system-wide sentiment anchor independent of any financial intermediary's profitability

Listed here only to make the macro/company distinction explicit; their bindings live in 'activations' and are unchanged.
